summary: Forest Service lookout on South Point, Skamania County, WA: 1933 L-4 tower, 41-foot tower from 1952, removed or destroyed in 1972; a radio tower and sheds stand on the summit.

facts.design: 5-foot wooden tower with L-4 cab (1933); 41-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab (1952 to 1972)
facts.status_note: Lookout tower removed or destroyed in 1972; sources disagree on which. A small radio tower and two sheds stand on the summit.

staffing.status: staffed in 1951 (Bob Baldwin); named as one of six retained lookouts for the 1964 season

access.note: Forest Service Trail 123 is open to hikers, horses and bicycles and closed to motorized use. No closure is named in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Trail 123 starts on Forest Road 20, 4.8 miles from Highway 12 west of Packwood, and climbs east to the former site through an old burn area. Trailhead space is limited. A 2023 trip report gives 7.7 miles round trip.

events.note: Panoramic photos taken from the site, July 26, 1934
Bob Baldwin performed fire observation duties during the fire season
41-foot timber tower with L-4 cab replaced the 1933 tower
Forest announced May 5, 1964 that 37 manned stations would be cut to six regularly manned lookouts; South Point was one of the six, mainly for communications
Removed per the register and the Forest Lookouts list
Destroyed per firelookout.com; WillhiteWeb gives April 3, 1972 and suggests it burned
Registered July 17, 2012 as US 1345, WA 245; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Removed in 1972 per the register and the Forest Lookouts list; destroyed in 1972 per firelookout.com; destroyed April 3, 1972, possibly by fire, per WillhiteWeb. The story reports the disagreement; no source settles it.

sources.title: South Point Lookout by Ives Peak in Gifford Pinchot National Forest

notes_for_editor: Brief checked: the 2012 registration, elevation and coordinates agree with the register. height_m 12.5 is the 1952 41-foot tower converted from feet; it is not a metric figure any source gives. The 1972 fate is disputed (removed vs destroyed, possibly burned). Bob Baldwin's 1951 service appears on three lookout-history pages; the Forest Lookouts page marks it as a personal conversation. WillhiteWeb's 1964 paragraph names Smith Point where the Forest Lookouts quotation of the Longview Daily News names South Point; the story follows South Point. The summit's current state rests on a 2023 trip report and a WillhiteWeb page of unknown date. No Forest Service page read describes the summit radio site. Trail 123 page last updated August 5, 2025.
